blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose NotchNook if you want widgets, live actions, deeper customization, notchless-screen support, and a larger device allowance. Choose Gojo if you want a focused MacBook surface for music, window snapping, clipboard history, files, and Night Shift.
points: Best for customization and widgets: NotchNook.
Best for a focused daily-control workflow: Gojo.
Both offer monthly and one-time purchase options.

blocks.text: Choose NotchNook for a configurable utility center

content.s: NotchNook calls itself a center of utilities and emphasizes widgets, live actions, a file shelf, scrolling gestures, multiple monitors, and many options. It is the stronger fit when customization and a larger notch environment are the point.

blocks.text: Choose Gojo for a smaller daily loop

content.s: Gojo is built around a repeatable set of actions: control music, snap a window, recover clipboard text, stage a file, or change display warmth. It is the better fit when you want the notch useful without filling it with a large widget system.

Gojo plans start at an introductory $2.99 per month or $9.99 lifetime for one Mac; 3-Mac plans are $4.99 per month or $19.99 lifetime. Every plan includes a fully unlocked 3-day trial. NotchNook's official page lists $3 per month or $25 for a one-time purchase, plus a 15-day refund window. Prices can change, so verify them before buying.
. Recommendations are based on workflow fit, published pricing, device limits, and product scope.
